# Percentage Composition in Chemistry – NMDCAT Prep

## Concept Breakdown

**Percentage composition** tells you what *fraction* (expressed as a percentage) of a compound's total molar mass is contributed by each individual element. It answers the question: *"If I have 1 mole of this compound, how many grams come from element X?"*

### The Core Formula

$$\% \text{ of element} = \left( \frac{\text{mass of that element in 1 mole of compound}}{\text{molar mass of the compound}} \right) \times 100$$

### Worked Example (MCQ-style)

**Compound:** H₂O (water)

| Step | Detail |
|---|---|
| Molar mass of H₂O | (2 × 1) + 16 = **18 g mol⁻¹** |
| Mass of H in 1 mol | 2 × 1 = **2 g** |
| Mass of O in 1 mol | 1 × 16 = **16 g** |
| % H | (2 / 18) × 100 ≈ **11.11 %** |
| % O | (16 / 18) × 100 ≈ **88.89 %** |
| Sanity check | 11.11 + 88.89 = **100 %** ✓ |

### Quick MCQ Tips
- Always start from the **chemical formula**; never guess.
- Multiply atomic mass by the **subscript count**.
- Add up all elements to get molar mass, then divide each element's contribution by that total.
- The percentages **must sum to 100 %**—use this to verify your answer.
- Watch for distractors that use **atomic mass alone** instead of the element's *total* contribution (e.g., forgetting to multiply by 2 for H in H₂O).

---

## GRINDEmap (Chunkmap)

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  G – GOAL                                                    │
│  Calculate the mass % each element contributes to a        │
│  compound's molar mass.                                     │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  R – ROOT / WHY IT MATTERS                                  │
│  • Determines elemental purity, stoichiometry,             │
│    empirical-formula work.                                 │
│  • Foundation for gravimetric & titration problems in      │
│    NMDCAT Chemistry.                                       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  I – INPUTS (what you need before you start)               │
│  ① Chemical formula (e.g. CaCO₃, Na₂SO₄)                  │
│  ② Atomic masses from the periodic table                  │
│  ③ Molar mass of the whole compound                        │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  N – NODES (key sub-concepts to chunk)                     │
│  N1  Atomic mass → mass of element in 1 mol of compound     │
│  N2  Molar mass of compound (sum of all element-masses)    │
│  N3  Fraction  =  (element mass) / (compound molar mass)   │
│  N4  Percentage  =  fraction × 100                         │
│  N5  Verification: Σ(%) must equal 100 %                  │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  D – DIRECTION (step-by-step process)                       │
│  Step 1  Write the formula; list each element & subscript.  │
│  Step 2  Multiply each atomic mass by its subscript count.  │
│  Step 3  Sum all → molar mass of compound.                  │
│  Step 4  For target element:  (its mass / molar mass)×100.  │
│  Step 5  Repeat for every element; check they sum to 100.  │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  E – EXAMPLES / PRACTICE                                    │
│  • H₂O  →  H ≈ 11.1 %,  O ≈ 88.9 %                        │
│  • CO₂  →  C ≈ 27.3 %,  O ≈ 72.7 %                        │
│  • CaCO₃ →  Ca ≈ 40 %,  C ≈ 12 %,  O ≈ 48 %               │
│  • Na₂SO₄→  Na ≈ 32.4 %, S ≈ 23.1 %, O ≈ 44.6 %            │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

> **Retention hook:** Think of it as a *pizza slice*. The whole pie = molar mass. Each element is a slice. Percentage composition is simply: *my slice / whole pie × 100*.

---

## Constrained Paragraph (three-vowel rule: **A – E – I** only)

> Each element in a chemical name takes a set rate. The aim is: find the part-rate, and raise it near a percent rate. The key is: be precise. In a plain state, the part-rate can be set near a percent rate. The idea is: take the rate: a part, and raise it near a percent rate. The name: water, is a clear case. The rate: a part, can be set near a percent rate. The aim is: take the rate: a part, and raise it near a percent rate.

*(Every word above contains only the vowels **A, E, I** — no O, no U.)*

---
